title: SECTION 1, UNIT 3
subtitle: Distinguish release mechanisms, prefix conjugates, and sound-alike suffixes (Adderall XR, ado-trastuzumab, Advair/Advicor).

lasaPairs.feature: Initial Ad- vs In- with identical -deral cadence

levels.title: Release & Suffix LASA Recognition
levels.description: Differentiate modified-release modifiers, prefix conjugates, and deceptive brand suffixes.
levels.learningObjective: Identify look-alike and sound-alike counterparts differing by suffixes and delivery modifiers.

activities.learningObjective: Distinguish look-alike suffixes and release modifiers from verified ISMP pairs.

questions.prompt: Which medication is the documented Look-Alike / Sound-Alike counterpart to Actonel?
questions.explanation: Actonel (risedronate) and Actos (pioglitazone) share deceptive initial letters and syllable cadence.

questions.prompt: Which formulation suffix designates the extended-release counterpart to immediate-release Adderall?
questions.explanation: Adderall XR designates the extended-release formulation, whereas Adderall alone indicates immediate-release.

questions.prompt: Which cardiovascular beta-blocker is an ISMP sound-alike counterpart to the stimulant Adderall?
questions.explanation: Adderall and Inderal share the identical '-deral' acoustic cadence and are easily confused in verbal communications.

questions.prompt: Which antibody-drug conjugate is the high-alert look-alike counterpart to conventional trastuzumab?
questions.explanation: ado-trastuzumab emtansine has the prefix 'ado-' and contains a cytotoxic conjugate, making confusion with conventional trastuzumab potentially fatal.

questions.prompt: Which medication is the sound-alike counterpart to Advair?
questions.explanation: Advair and Advicor share look-alike prefixes and sound-alike syllables.

questions.prompt: Which cholesterol drug pairs with Advicor on the ISMP list?
questions.explanation: Advicor and Altocor differ only in middle letters (-dvi- vs -lto-).

levels.title: Interactive Pair Matching
levels.description: Connect look-alike and sound-alike counterparts through interactive active-retrieval matching.
levels.learningObjective: Reinforce memory links between confusable pairs through tactile matching practice.

activities.learningObjective: Identify documented counterpart relationships before matching.

questions.prompt: Which medication is the sound-alike counterpart to Actonel?
questions.explanation: Actonel and Actos look and sound similar.

questions.prompt: Which suffix designates the extended-release counterpart to Adderall?
questions.explanation: Adderall XR designates extended-release.

questions.prompt: Which drug is a sound-alike counterpart to Adderall?
questions.explanation: Adderall and Inderal share acoustic cadence.

questions.prompt: Which conjugate drug pairs with conventional trastuzumab?
questions.explanation: ado-trastuzumab emtansine carries a cytotoxic conjugate.

activities.learningObjective: Match each medication with its documented confusable counterpart.

questions.prompt: Match each medication with its documented ISMP confusable counterpart:
questions.explanation: Actonel/Actos, Adderall/Adderall XR, ado-trastuzumab/trastuzumab, and Advair/Advicor are verified ISMP 2023 confusable pairs.

questions.prompt: Match each medication with its confusable suffix or extension counterpart:
questions.explanation: Adderall/Inderal, Advicor/Altocor, and Afrin active/saline are documented ISMP pairs.

levels.title: Brand Extension & Suffix Discrimination
levels.description: Discriminate deceptive brand line extensions and confusable respiratory/lipid suffixes.
levels.learningObjective: Differentiate brand name suffixes (Advair vs Advicor) and brand line extensions (Afrin formulations).

activities.learningObjective: Differentiate brand extension qualifiers and multi-ingredient suffixes.

questions.prompt: Which lipid-regulating medication name is an ISMP look-alike / sound-alike counterpart to the inhaler Advair?
questions.explanation: Advair (fluticasone/salmeterol) and Advicor (niacin/lovastatin) share deceptive prefix and syllable flow.

questions.prompt: Which cholesterol medication name pairs with Advicor on the ISMP list of confused drug names?
questions.explanation: Advicor and Altocor differ only in middle letters (-dvi- vs -lto-) and both involve lovastatin.

questions.prompt: Which ingredient distinction separates the decongestant Afrin from its non-medicated counterpart on the ISMP list?
questions.explanation: Brand extension confusion occurs when Afrin containing active oxymetazoline is confused with plain Afrin saline nasal mist.

questions.prompt: Which drug is the sound-alike counterpart to Actonel?
questions.explanation: Actonel and Actos sound alike.

questions.prompt: Which conjugate drug pairs with conventional trastuzumab?
questions.explanation: ado-trastuzumab emtansine carries a cytotoxic conjugate.

questions.prompt: Which formulation suffix designates extended-release Adderall?

questions.prompt: Which beta-blocker is a sound-alike counterpart to Adderall?
